data.name: 7 days with Death
data.detailed_description:
New information


New project "Lingua Fleur: Lily" is COOMING SOON!


Acerca do jogo

In 2013, Narrator released its fourth game focusing on fate and choice.
Through cooperation with SSCP, the quality of this game has improved over our previous works!

Containing the 3 original routes, plus an additional route, the script length is about 130,000 words in total.
Featuring 19 CGs, a soundtrack of 9 songs plus the main Chinese theme song, and stunning backgrounds based on Taiwan's Tamsui District (淡水).

※ This game does not have character voices

story:

"In seven days, you will die."
On Christmas Eve, a strange girl breaks into your home claiming to be the bringer of death.
"I will be with you for seven days... if you don't want to die, you must find someone who is willing to die for you."
This unbelievable prophesy is then followed by many strange omens...

Daily life becomes unpredictable, even to the point where he runs into Shaw Chin, who had just ended a relationship.
Is she someone who will love me... who will die for me?
Death haunts his every move.

On New Years Eve, Death looms over him.
As the fireworks light up the night sky, he must make a choice...

reviews.review:
7 Days with Death is a visual novel that builds its tension around a chillingly simple premise: on Christmas Eve, a mysterious girl breaks into the protagonist’s home and calmly tells him that he will die in seven days. From that moment, every interaction and every decision is shaped by the looming countdown, and the game uses this structure to keep players engaged with a mix of dread, curiosity, and the faint hope that fate can somehow be altered. The story wastes no time in pulling the player into its eerie atmosphere, balancing the mundane rhythms of daily life with the constant intrusion of the supernatural.

The narrative unfolds across several routes, each offering different perspectives on the central mystery. There are multiple endings to uncover, and the way you interact with the characters around you determines which path you will take. Some choices feel small in the moment but ripple out into major consequences later on, giving the sense that you are truly shaping the protagonist’s fate. The branching design makes replaying rewarding, especially on the first few runs, as new layers of character and story emerge depending on who you align with and how you respond to the girl who brings death. The game’s script is lengthy and deliberate, taking time to develop its cast before building toward its climax, and the sense of an approaching deadline keeps the tension sharp even during slower passages.

A striking element of the experience is how the supernatural collides with the everyday. Much of the story takes place in ordinary settings and revolves around common interactions, but the presence of death always hangs over them, making the ordinary feel fragile. This contrast between daily life and looming mortality creates unease and forces the player to consider how quickly the familiar can collapse. The art reinforces this tone with carefully drawn backgrounds inspired by real places, paired with character designs that are expressive without being overly flashy. The addition of CG scenes at key story moments heightens the drama, punctuating important choices and revelations with memorable visuals.

The sound design complements the mood, using a modest but effective soundtrack that shifts between subtle ambient tracks and more dramatic themes as events escalate. While the game lacks voice acting, the writing and atmosphere carry the weight of the story. For some players, the absence of spoken dialogue may limit the emotional punch of certain moments, but others may appreciate the quieter, text-driven style that leaves more to imagination. The pacing is strongest in the final days of the countdown, when choices become heavier and the narrative pushes toward multiple possible conclusions, each colored by the relationships you have built and the sacrifices you are willing to accept.

Despite its strengths, the game is not without flaws. Some routes feel stronger and more satisfying than others, and there are moments where character motivations or supernatural elements are left ambiguous or underexplored. The branching structure, while central to the experience, also means that sections of dialogue and events are reused across playthroughs, which can make later replays feel repetitive. For players who want a highly polished narrative where every path is equally compelling, this unevenness may be noticeable. Still, the moments where the writing clicks—especially when the weight of death bears down and the stakes feel real—make the journey worthwhile.

7 Days with Death ultimately succeeds as a moody and memorable visual novel that combines existential dread with human connection. It does not rely on spectacle or heavy mechanics, but instead on the power of choice, atmosphere, and the inevitability of time running out. For those who enjoy visual novels that mix supernatural themes with emotional stakes, it offers a unique and engaging experience, one that lingers after the screen fades to black. It is a game best suited for players who value story above all else and who don’t mind replaying to see all possible outcomes, even if not every branch reaches the same narrative heights.

Rating: 8/10
